name: John M. Dolan
title: Principal Systems Scientist
department: Robotics Institute; DRIVE Lab affiliated with Electrical and Computer Engineering
fitReason: DRIVE has concrete learning-to-control research on actual vehicles, combined with current transformer-control research. The live external-graduate visitor inquiry route makes this a useful lead for a focused robot-learning summer project, although eight weeks is not explicitly approved.

physicalEvidence.summary: The March 2025 revision of Agile Mobility deploys a meta-learned LSTM dynamics model with uncertainty-aware MPPI on a physical RC car. Tests cover towing, taped/plastic tyres, surface changes and steering bias. The source links the DRIVE-LAB-CMU implementation, and current lab records identify first author Dvij Kalaria as a former supervised master’s student. September 2026 transformer-control work is theoretical/simulated and is not counted as another physical experiment.

shortVisit.summary: The live Contact page, dated August 20, 2026, explicitly invites non-CMU graduate students interested in visiting research to email Dolan. Its introductory invitation includes master’s students. The separate undergraduate instruction points to RISS. Duration, funding, summer 2027 capacity and final university eligibility are unspecified.

scoreReasons.fit: Strong embodied learning and adaptive control, mainly wheeled robotics rather than manipulation/VLA.
scoreReasons.physical: Real learned-model deployment tied directly to current lab through author repository and supervised student.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Live explicit external graduate visitor instruction includes master’s context; dates/duration/funding unspecified.
scoreReasons.freshness: Current August 2026 lab update and explicit September 2026 primary research; hardware revision separately dated 2025.

unknowns: His exact official appointment is Principal Systems Scientist. CMU lists him in faculty, names him DRIVE head and lists advised students; the record does not relabel him as a professorial rank.

The RC-car paper compares several controllers; the proposed learned method is not superior in every hardware configuration. High-speed full-size racing and Mars/mud scenarios elsewhere on lab pages or in the paper are not all physical validation of this method.

The learned model informs MPPI planning rather than directly outputting an end-to-end language-conditioned action policy. The physical manuscript began in 2024 and was revised in March 2025; current activity is independently evidenced in 2026.

Existing CMU OIE review supports a foreign-degree Student Intern route with personal/outside support in principle, but eight-week dates and appointment remain subject to OIE and department approval. Collaborating Visitor screening is a separate required process and does not provide visa support.

Summer 2027 acceptance, mentor capacity, exact dates, funding, visitor appointment, and applicable university/immigration approvals remain unconfirmed. Self-funding alone does not establish eligibility.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
Institutional appointment and screening remain separate from the PI inquiry: [CMU research-visitor notes](../eligibility_notes.md#cmu-student-intern).
